avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (high dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: PPIs reduce gastric acid, impairing calcium absorption; concurrent high-dose supplementation may not compensate for reduced bioavailability and increase hypercalcemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2+ hours; use lower doses or food-based sources; monitor calcium levels periodically

avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Pantoprazole increases gastric pH, significantly reducing iron absorption (up to 66% reduction)
avoid_supplements.action: Separate by at least 2 hours; consider alternative PPI timing or supplemental form; monitor for anemia

avoid_supplements.name: Vitamin B12 supplements (if long-term use)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Chronic PPI use reduces intrinsic factor and gastric acid needed for B12 absorption; supplementation may be needed but efficacy is reduced
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels annually with long-term pantoprazole use; consider sublingual or intramuscular B12 dosing

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: PPIs can reduce magnesium absorption; long-term deficiency risk exists but acute interactions are minimal
caution_supplements.action: Monitor magnesium levels; space dosing 2+ hours apart; consider food-based sources

caution_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
caution_supplements.mechanism: Moderate CYP3A4 inducer may slightly reduce pantoprazole efficacy through increased metabolism
caution_supplements.action: Monitor symptom control; may require pantoprazole dose adjustment if combined therapy necessary

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals (concurrent with dosing)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Fat delays gastric emptying and reduces pantoprazole absorption when taken with food
avoid_foods.action: Take pantoprazole 30-60 minutes before meals; separate from high-fat foods at time of administration

caution_foods.name: Calcium-rich foods (dairy, fortified products)
caution_foods.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid may modestly impair calcium bioavailability from food sources, but clinical impact is minimal with balanced diet
caution_foods.action: Encourage adequate dietary calcium intake; monitor for signs of deficiency with long-term PPI use

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Pantoprazole reduces acid-stimulated gastric secretion; caffeine effects on acid production may be blunted, reducing symptom relief benefit but not creating direct interaction
caution_foods.action: Monitor symptom control; reduce caffeine if reflux worsens; no absolute contraindication

monitoring_notes: Long-term pantoprazole use (>1 year) warrants periodic monitoring of vitamin B12, magnesium, and calcium levels, especially in elderly patients or those with malabsorption risk factors. PPIs significantly reduce absorption of iron and calcium; counsel patients on optimal timing and consider supplementation strategies accordingly.
